mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5% in a month triggers a decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant negative deviation from the pre-inflation spike mean (t-test p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS remains below 5% for 60 days after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) correlates with stronger consumer demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or PAYEMS growth decelerates for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) below their 12-month moving averages predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as demand softens.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain non-negative over 10 consecutive such signals or the IC > 0.05 for the interaction term.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in INDPRO (industrial production) above 105 suggests supply-side expansion, which usually precedes S&P 500 positive 20-day forward returns in normal regimes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite INDPRO > 105 for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for 3 consecutive months, it signals labor market strength and typically drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or UNRATE rebounds above 4% within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in GDPC1 (GDP) growth exceeding +6% in a quarter interacts with low CPIAUCSL (inflation) to produce positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as growth is seen as broad-based and inflation remains controlled.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +6% in a quarter and CPIAUCSL < 3% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or CPIAUCSL > 3% in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2%, S&P 500 5-day forward returns tend to be positive as investors anticipate rate cuts and demand expansion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative or CPIAUCSL does not sustain below 2% for 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and HOUST show double-digit declines in the same month, it indicates sector-specific supply disruptions that are associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or both INDPRO and HOUST recover in the following month.
